title: Cleopatra
objective: After this level you can explain who Cleopatra was and how she ruled.
summary: Cleopatra VII came from a Macedonian Greek dynasty but learned Egyptian. She ruled from 51 to 30 BCE, allied with Caesar and Antony, and lost to Octavian.

cards.headline: Cleopatra came from a line of kings who never learned Egyptian.
cards.body: According to Plutarch, the kings before her hadn’t even tried. Cleopatra did. That tells you a lot about how she ruled.

cards.headline: Greek by family, Egyptian by choice
cards.body: Cleopatra VII was born in 70 or 69 BCE into the Ptolemies, a royal family of Macedonian Greek descent. Plutarch says she learned Egyptian and switched languages so easily that she seldom needed an interpreter. For political reasons she also styled herself the new Isis, after the Egyptian goddess. She didn’t just rule Egypt; she spoke to it.

cards.headline: A queen against Rome
cards.body: She ruled from 51 to 30 BCE. Forced out by her brother Ptolemy XIII, she regained power with Julius Caesar’s help and had a son by him, Caesarion. Later she allied with Mark Antony. In 31 BCE Octavian defeated them at the Battle of Actium, and in 30 BCE she died. Legend says by an asp’s bite; how she really died is uncertain. That same year, Egypt became a Roman province.

cards.headline: What did she look like?
cards.body: Nobody knows for sure. A coin from her alliance with Antony shows both of them with beaked noses and jutting chins, like her Ptolemaic ancestors: a political image, not a photograph. Her mother isn’t known for certain, so part of her family tree is a question mark. And Plutarch wrote that her beauty alone wasn’t incomparable; her conversation was what charmed people.

cards.headline: Cleopatra: met
learned: Cleopatra VII came from a Macedonian Greek dynasty
She learned Egyptian and styled herself the new Isis
Allied with Caesar and Antony, she lost to Octavian at Actium

questions.prompt: What set Cleopatra apart from the Ptolemaic kings before her, according to Plutarch?

options.label: She was the first born in Egypt
She was the first to marry a Roman
options.rationale: Plutarch’s contrast was that the earlier kings never learned Egyptian.

questions.explanation: Plutarch says earlier kings had not even tried to learn Egyptian; Cleopatra did, and seldom needed an interpreter.

questions.prompt: Why can’t we say exactly what Cleopatra looked like?

options.label: No images of her were ever made
Her coins are political images, and even her mother isn’t certain
Her mummy shows her face clearly
Plutarch described her face in exact, careful detail
options.rationale: He talked about her conversation instead.

questions.explanation: Her coin portraits were official images, part of her ancestry is unknown, and ancient writers praised her charm more than her looks.

questions.prompt: Cleopatra died in 30 BCE. From Level 1, what happened to Egypt that same year?

options.label: It was united for the first time
It became a province of Rome

questions.explanation: Cleopatra’s death in 30 BCE closed ancient Egypt’s roughly 3,000-year story: Egypt became a Roman province.
